prompt: Stage 2-5, level 5, 90 HP, 19 gold. Your five board units include a 1-star 2-cost caster with no synergy. On the bench sits a 2-star 1-cost bruiser, also without synergy, that you were 'keeping until something better'. What goes on the board this round?

options.label: Put the 2-star bruiser on the board in place of the 1-star caster; a 2-star 1-cost beats a 1-star 2-cost
Keep the caster: a 2-cost is a stronger unit than a 1-cost, and it might pair
Sell the 2-star bruiser: a 1-cost will not be in your final board

explanation:
Strongest board every round means the strongest units, not the most expensive ones. A 2-star has roughly 80% more health and damage than its 1-star, and a 2-star 1-cost is stronger than a 1-star 2-cost in almost every matchup: the cost step is smaller than the star step. The bruiser also goes in the front line where a second body helps your tank, while the caster is a back-row unit that dies when the front folds.

'It might pair' is not a reason to field it: pairs sit on the bench fine, and this caster has no synergy and one copy. Selling the bruiser is the other extreme, throwing away 3 gold of board strength for a final board that is stages away. Every stage-2 fight you lose with a weaker board is HP you never get back; every unit on the bench that would beat a unit on the board is a fight you chose to lose.
principle: The strongest unit plays, and a 2-star 1-cost is stronger than a 1-star 2-cost. Cost is not strength.
commonMistake: Fielding a 1-star because it costs more, while a 2-star of a cheaper unit waits on the bench 'for later'.
hint: Compare what a star-up does to a unit's stats against what one cost level does. Then ask which of the two units survives longer in a fight.
